policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'there is gathered unto him' is present tense, matching the present συνάγεται; the aorist συνήχθη would give 'there was gathered'.
ASV 'a very great multitude' renders the superlative πλεῖστος; plain πολύς would be 'a great multitude'.
ASV 'he entered into a boat' is indefinite, matching anarthrous εἰς πλοῖον; the RP reading has the article τὸ πλοῖον ('the boat').
ASV 'all the multitude were by the sea' uses a plural verb, matching ἦσαν; singular ἦν would give 'was' (as KJV has).
ASV 'went forth to sow' renders the purpose infinitive alike with or without the articular τοῦ; the added article leaves no trace in English.
ASV opens 'And other fell'; ASV routinely renders postpositive δέ as 'and', so the connective does not distinguish καὶ ἄλλο from Ἄλλο δέ.
ASV 'on the rocky ground, where it had not much earth' has no conjunction before the relative clause, matching bare ὅπου rather than καὶ ὅπου.
εὐθύς and εὐθέως are the same word in two forms; ASV 'straightway' renders either.
ASV 'and when the sun was risen' renders a ὅτε clause and a genitive absolute alike, and 'and' serves for either καί or δέ.
ASV 'it was scorched' is singular, matching ἐκαυματίσθη; the plural ἐκαυματίσθησαν would give 'they were scorched'.
ASV 'And others fell into the good ground' is plural, matching ἄλλα; singular ἄλλο would be 'other fell' as in v.5 and v.7.
ASV 'others ... growing up and increasing' requires plural participles, excluding singular αὐξανόμενον; the middle αὐξανόμενα and active αὐξάνοντα are indistinguishable in 'increasing'.
ASV 'thirtyfold, and sixtyfold, and a hundredfold' renders only the numerals; the ἕν/εἰς/ἐν forms of the distributive leave no distinguishing trace in the English.
ASV 'Who hath ears to hear' uses a relative with a finite verb, matching Ὃς ἔχει; the participial Ὁ ἔχων would give 'He that hath'.
ASV 'And when he was alone' fits both Καὶ ὅτε and Ὅτε δέ, since ASV commonly renders δέ as 'and'.
ASV 'asked of him the parables' is a simple past that renders imperfect ἠρώτων and aorist ἠρώτησαν alike.
ASV 'the parables' is plural, matching τὰς παραβολάς; τὴν παραβολήν would give 'the parable'.
ASV 'Unto you is given the mystery of the kingdom of God' has no infinitive of knowing; the RP reading's γνῶναι would require 'to know the mystery'.
ASV 'and it should be forgiven them' ends with the pronoun and supplies no object; the RP addition τὰ ἁμαρτήματα would give 'their sins should be forgiven them'.
εὐθύς and εὐθέως are alternative forms of one word; ASV 'straightway' renders either.
ASV 'the word which hath been sown in them' matches εἰς αὐτούς; the RP reading ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις αὐτῶν would give 'in their hearts'.
ASV 'And these in like manner are they' renders ὁμοίως explicitly; the NA omission would leave the phrase untranslated.
ASV 'straightway' renders εὐθύς and εὐθέως alike.
ASV 'straightway they stumble' renders εὐθύς and εὐθέως alike.
ASV 'And others are they that are sown among the thorns' renders ἄλλοι; οὗτοί would give 'these', which ASV instead uses for the following clause.
ASV has a second clause 'these are they that have heard the word', rendering οὗτοί εἰσιν; the RP omission leaves no such demonstrative and copula.
ASV 'that have heard the word' is past-referring, matching aorist ἀκούσαντες; present ἀκούοντες would give 'that hear the word', as ASV renders the present in v.20.
ASV 'the cares of the world' has no demonstrative, excluding the RP addition τούτου ('this world'); the mapped gloss 'Or, age' shows the noun rendered is αἰών, not βίος, which ASV renders 'life'.
ASV 'And those are they that were sown' renders the far demonstrative ἐκεῖνοι; οὗτοί would give 'these', as in v.18.
ASV 'thirtyfold, and sixtyfold, and a hundredfold' renders only the numerals; the ἕν/ἐν forms of the distributive leave no trace in the English.
The WH addition is recitative ὅτι introducing direct speech, which ASV leaves untranslated after 'And he said unto them'.
The variant is word order only; ASV 'Is the lamp brought' renders either arrangement of ἔρχεται ὁ λύχνος.
ASV 'to be put on the stand' takes its 'on' from ἐπὶ τὴν λυχνίαν and renders simple τεθῇ and compound ἐπιτεθῇ alike.
ASV 'there is nothing hid, save that it should be manifested' has no relative clause; the RP reading τι κρυπτόν, ὃ ἐὰν μὴ φανερωθῇ would give 'anything hid, which shall not be manifested'.
ASV 'but that it should come to light' renders the purpose conjunction ἵνα, which the omitting reading lacks.
The variant is word order only; ASV 'that it should come to light' renders either arrangement of ἔλθῃ εἰς φανερόν.
ASV 'and more shall be given unto you' ends without an apposition; the RP addition τοῖς ἀκούουσιν would give 'unto you that hear'.
ASV 'For he that hath' is a permissible rendering of both the plain relative with ἔχει and the generalizing ὃς ἂν ἔχῃ.
ASV 'even that which he hath' is neuter, matching ὅ; the masculine ὅς would give 'he who hath'.
ASV 'as if a man should cast seed' supplies the conditional sense; both ὡς and ὡς ἐάν with the subjunctive yield that rendering.
βλαστᾷ and βλαστάνῃ are alternative present subjunctive forms of one verb; ASV 'should spring up' renders either.
ASV 'The earth beareth fruit of herself' has no causal connective; the RP addition γάρ would be rendered 'for'.
εἶτα and εἶτεν are spelling variants of one adverb; ASV 'then ... then' renders either.
ASV 'the full grain in the ear' shows neither the case of σῖτον/σῖτος nor the form of πλήρης/πλήρη.
παραδοῖ and παραδῷ are alternative subjunctive forms of one verb; ASV 'is ripe' (note 'Or, alloweth') renders either.
ASV 'straightway' renders εὐθύς and εὐθέως alike.
ASV 'How shall we liken the kingdom of God?' renders the adverb Πῶς; the RP reading Τίνι would give 'To what shall we liken'.
ASV 'in what parable' renders τίνι and ποίᾳ alike, both being 'what' with the noun.
ASV 'shall we set it forth' renders θῶμεν; the RP verb παραβάλωμεν would give 'shall we compare it'.
The mapped gloss 'Greek As unto' shows the comparison stands with ὡς and a dative, matching κόκκῳ rather than the accusative κόκκον.
ASV's concessive 'though it be less than all the seeds' renders the participle ὄν; the RP μικρότερος without participle stands in a plain relative clause.
ASV 'though it be less than all the seeds that are upon the earth' supplies the copula in English either way; an added ἐστίν leaves no separate trace.
ASV 'becometh greater than all the herbs' shows neither the gender of μεῖζον/μείζων nor the word order of the phrase.
ASV 'privately to his own disciples' renders ἰδίοις; μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ would give simply 'his disciples'.
ASV 'And other boats were with him' uses the same noun as 'the boat' earlier in the verse, matching πλοῖα; the diminutive πλοιάρια would give 'little ships' (so KJV).
The variant is word order only; ASV 'a great storm of wind' renders either arrangement.
ASV 'and the waves beat into the boat' fits both καὶ τά and τὰ δέ, since ASV commonly renders δέ as 'and'.
ASV 'insomuch that the boat was now filling' names the noun τὸ πλοῖον; the RP reading has the pronoun αὐτό, which would give 'it was now filling'.
The variant is word order only; ASV 'And he himself was in the stern' renders either arrangement of αὐτὸς ἦν.
ASV 'in the stern' renders ἐν; ἐπί with the dative would give 'on' or 'at the stern'.
ASV 'they awake him' renders simple ἐγείρουσιν and compound διεγείρουσιν alike.
ASV 'have ye not yet faith?' renders οὔπω; the RP reading οὕτως Πῶς οὐκ would give 'so fearful? how have ye no faith?'.
ASV 'even the wind and the sea obey him' shows no number for the verb, since English 'obey' serves for singular ὑπακούει with a compound subject and for plural ὑπακούουσιν.
